newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bid values Suez minimum 280 Ffr/shr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bid values Suez minimum 280 Ffr/shr - paper.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux will absorb Cie de Suez, whose shares would be valued at a minimum of 280 francs, the French newspaper Les Echos reported on Thursday.

Citing unnamed sources close to the deal, the newspaper said Belgian businessman Albert Frere, who owns eight percent of Suez through Electrafina, had approved the deal, which would be presented to the boards of Suez and Lyonnaise next week.

It said Belgian authorities had also given their approval after Suez assured them that its indirectly controlled subsidiary Tractebel would keep its headquarters in Belgium and would remain listed on the Brussels bourse.

Les Echos said Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod would be chairman initially, and Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet would be vice chairman. It said Monod had been scheduled to retire from Lyonnaise in 1998 when he turned 70, "and that rule may apply to the new Lyonnaise-Suez".
"According to our sources, the majority of the major shareholders have given their approval to the structure of the deal," it said.
"It should lead to the absorption of Suez by Lyonnaise, but without going through a share exchange offer".
It said a source close to the deal said Suez shares would be valued "at a minimum of 280 francs".
